close_reason: Moot after sgrr.4 dropped the JsContactId newtype (commit 6cf54bc). No type exists to add a validate() helper to. The 'character-set validation is the caller's responsibility' contract is now documented as a property of the bare-String approach in README.md Gotchas and on the per-field doc-comments.
description:
lib.rs:51-63 defines JsContactId with the doc-comment:

  'A string of 1–255 octets containing only base64url-safe characters
   (A-Z, a-z, 0-9, -, _). JSContact Id values are NOT JMAP Id values:
   validation of the character set is left to the caller because this
   crate has no JMAP dependency.'

The contract is documented but the crate ships zero help for honouring it. A
caller building a JsContactId from untrusted input (e.g. a deserialized
ContactCard) must implement the regex / character-class check themselves to
catch values that exceed 255 octets or contain disallowed characters. Every
consumer ends up writing the same 10-line check.

The 'no JMAP dependency' rationale is sound for not importing jmap_types::Id —
but a local fn validate(s: &str) -> Result<(), JsContactIdError> on this
crate is pure-Rust and adds no dependency. Likewise a TryFrom<String> /
TryFrom<&str> impl that runs the check.

Current From<String> and From<&str> impls accept any string silently, so a
caller cannot rely on JsContactId carrying a valid value at the type level.
The newtype is decorative.

Fix: add either a validate() inherent method or TryFrom impls (or both — TryFrom
for strict construction, From for unchecked, with a clear naming convention).

This makes the validation 'left to the caller' line in the doc-comment a
genuine contract instead of a hand-wave.
title: JsContactId character-set validation deferred to caller but no validate() helper provided
